head: 36ea28ab28fd93258143ab4312e60e2b5e244843

source.ref: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/75218; AACR-Bench dataset.json rows 1045, 1047; hand-checked 2026-10-23 by adjudicator after two blind vetters; licence Apache-2.0 read from LICENSE at head; the pull request's commit 5f3596784ad, after head, replaced the remaining assert with chassert, and master keeps chassert in all four pop methods

rationale: A compile-time refactor that moves Identifier's and IdentifierView's constructors and pop methods from the header into Identifier.cpp and turns their asserts into chassert. row-1047 is true at head and the author fixed it in the same pull request (author-fix), but it stays optional: the check in IdentifierView::popLast behaves exactly as it did at base and only misses the sanitizer-build coverage its three siblings gained, so no build behaves worse; the reference's second half (move the methods back to the header for inlining) is a design choice the pull request rejected on purpose and upstream kept, so it is dropped, and the range is narrowed to the method's head and assertion. row-1045 is false at head: both full-name constructors fill parts by splitting the member full_name in their bodies (the person's comment on that line was a formatting suggestion, which AACR-Bench restated as a missing initialization). Following ADR-0036's lvgl precedent, the claim is retired for a vetting defect and its range becomes a forbid range: AACR-Bench's annotators accepted the misreading, and the rvalue overload, which splits right after a std::move, is a common use-after-move false positive. Adjudicated: vetter A kept the case as forbid plus one optional claim, vetter B dropped it for lack of a forbid range; the adjudicator sides with A. forbid-seeds.json has no entries for this pull request; the rest of the change only moves includes.

expect.concern: IdentifierView::popLast keeps a plain assert where the three other moved pop methods now use chassert, so sanitizer builds compiled with NDEBUG do not catch a call that removes more parts than the view holds, which moves parts_end_it before parts_start_it.

forbid.reason: Both full-name constructors fill parts in their bodies by splitting the already-initialized member full_name, not the moved-from parameter, so a finding that parts is left empty or that the split reads a moved-from string is false.
